prompt: I have only used a little Python. If TypeScript removes the types, can a string still end up in a number variable?
source: TypeScript checks types before execution and erases type annotations. JavaScript executes the resulting program. Unvalidated external data, any, or type assertions can bypass static assurance. A type assertion does not validate or convert its value. For external data intended to be a finite number, a runtime check can test typeof value === 'number' and Number.isFinite(value).
facts: Types are erased before ordinary JavaScript execution.
External data or bypasses can violate the declared type.
Runtime validation is separate from an annotation or assertion.
forbidden: Claims TypeScript guarantees all runtime input types.
Claims an assertion converts or validates the value.
teaching: Answer the apparent contradiction with a concrete handle without a compiler architecture lecture.

prompt: 这个配置里的 retry: 3 是会创建三个任务吗？
source:
Synthetic fixture, not a real library. config.yaml: retry: 3
loader.py: cfg = yaml.safe_load(text); worker = Worker(max_retries=cfg['retry'])
Worker.run(job): makes one initial attempt; on failure, retries sequentially up to max_retries times, stopping on success; no parallel tasks are created. The constructor stores max_retries and does not start execution.
facts: The YAML value is parsed and passed into the constructor.
One Worker instance stores a retry limit; the constructor does not start jobs.
At most four sequential attempts including the first, stopping on success.
forbidden: Claims three workers or parallel jobs are created.
teaching: Resolve the object-count versus retry-count misconception in Chinese; connect the setting to the actual consumer.

source: Shared supplied learning context, identical for every arm; no real personal profile is used. General preference: detailed explanations. Project note at old revision: learned the request route and input validation; next read save_order in storage.py. Current synthetic repository: storage.py has been removed; app.py calls validate(payload), then repository.save_order(order), then format_reply(order_id). repository.py saves order in a dictionary and returns its integer id. The dictionary exists only in memory. Current request asks to continue briefly.
facts: Resume at repository.save_order after validation rather than restarting the lesson.
Use the current repository.py path, acknowledging the stale path if useful.
Explain save returns an integer id then format_reply uses it.
State storage is in-memory, not durable.

Lets the general detailed preference override the current brief request.
Claims a profile was saved or edited.
